conventions.convention: A Seifert surface is connected, compact, smooth, oriented and embedded, with oriented boundary equal to the specified knot. An outward conormal followed by a positive boundary tangent gives the surface orientation.
The diagram procedure takes a finite regular oriented diagram with exactly one component. It returns construction data; embeddedness and boundary correctness are separate conclusions.
Knot genus is the minimum over genera of admissible Seifert surfaces. The genus of a particular diagram surface supplies only an upper bound.
The inward unit surface conormal is the reference framing; the positive quarter-turn uses the oriented normal plane. Relative winding assigns this reference integer zero.
The zero-self-linking theorem assumes full Axiom of Choice, including for its linking-number-as-intersection supplier; the surface-construction and genus results assume countable choice.
Prescribed collar extensions agree at the same sufficiently small collar parameter, and the optional interior prescription is an orientation-preserving diffeomorphism germ.

load_bearing.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let D be a finite regular oriented diagram of a single knot, and let the Seifert algorithm supply its finite disk-and-band construction data. These disks and bands can be realized in S³ as a connected compact smooth oriented embedded surface F with exactly one boundary component, whose oriented boundary is the knot represented by D. The bands can be chosen mutually disjoint and disjoint from disk interiors except at their attaching intervals.
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Every smooth oriented knot K ⊂ S³ bounds a connected compact smooth oriented embedded surface F ⊂ S³ whose oriented boundary is K.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. For an oriented smooth knot K ⊂ S³, the smooth knot genus is g(K) := min G(K), where G(K) is the nonempty set of nonnegative integers realized as genera of Seifert surfaces for K.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. If a connected compact oriented disk-and-band surface F is built from s disjoint disks by attaching c rectangular bands along boundary intervals and has one boundary component, then χ(F) = s − c and g(F) = (1 − s + c)/2. For the Seifert-algorithm surface of an oriented knot diagram, g(K) ≤ (1 − s + c)/2.

Under countable choice, a smooth planar Jordan region is diffeomorphic to the closed standard disk. Every orientation-preserving smooth boundary diffeomorphism between two such regions extends to an orientation-preserving disk diffeomorphism, with the specified boundary-collar agreement and optional prescribed positive interior diffeomorphism germ.

For a smooth oriented knot with a supplied connected compact oriented smooth embedded spanning surface, the inward surface conormal gives a reference frame in which relative normal-field degree bijects framing classes with the integers. Adding n positive full twists changes this integer by n.

seams_checked.note: The framing theorem preserves the inward-conormal and normalized-push-off conventions. Its signed-intersection use retains full choice, supplies a regular diagram and uses the truncated surface with empty intersection in the correct component order.

Consumers use genus as an attained minimum over connected oriented spanning surfaces. The trefoil calculation uses the diagram formula only for its upper bound; minimality and the genus-zero characterization have separate arguments.
Consumers retain the smooth compact oriented spanning-surface hypotheses and χ(F) = 1 − 2g. Existence uses the stated theorem, and full-choice consumers discharge its countable-choice assumption.

Slice-genus nonemptiness pushes a supplied Seifert surface into the ball and preserves its genus. The four-dimensional intersection argument uses spanning-surface existence under its stronger full-choice hypothesis.

Consumers use supplied oriented Seifert surfaces and, where specified, minimum-genus surfaces for normalization. Analytic comparison and filtration claims are assigned to separate suppliers rather than inferred from the genus definition.

The reconstruction uniqueness proof uses exactly the smooth Jordan-disk extension with prescribed collars and an interior identity germ at infinity. It retains countable choice for smooth uniqueness and treats finite realization and enumeration separately.
